transcript.text: theres a funny smell from my oven when its on

A funny smell when an oven first heats up is often normal: new ovens burn off protective coatings for a few cycles, and any food residue will also smoke. However, we need to rule out a safety issue with the electrical connection at the back of the oven. Please check two things:
1. Does it smell like burning plastic or electrical insulation (a sharp, acrid smell)?
2. Is the smell coming from inside the cooking space, or is it strongest near the back wall where the power cable enters? If you smell burning plastic or see smoke/char marks at the back, switch the oven off immediately and do not use it again until an engineer checks the mains connection.

yeah more like hot plastic or electrical I think, and it seems to come from behind or underneath rather than inside the oven. no smoke that I've seen. lights flickered once too and I heard a crackle from the back once

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Given that the smell sounds like hot plastic/electrical insulation, comes from the back or underneath (where the power cable enters), and you’ve heard crackling with lights flickering, this points to a serious electrical issue—most likely an overheating mains terminal block or internal wiring fault. This is a fire hazard. Please switch off the oven at the wall/isolator immediately and do not use it again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has inspected the connection and internal wiring.
